original_question: For a finite group G, let χ1(G) denote the totality of the degrees of all irreducible complex characters of G with allowance for their multiplicities. Suppose that H is a finite group with χ1(H) = χ1(G). If G has trivial solvable radical, must H also have trivial solvable radical?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.135 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)". ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s official problem almost verbatim: it uses finite groups G and H, the notation χ1(X) for irreducible complex character degrees counted with multiplicity, the hypothesis χ1(H) = χ1(G), and the conclusion asking whether trivial solvable radical must then pass from G to H. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: Say explicitly that χ1(X) is a multiset (or totality) of character degrees, not the set of distinct degrees.
State that the characters are ordinary irreducible complex characters, i.e. χ ranges over Irr(X).
Make the quantifiers fully explicit: the question is about all finite groups G and H.
Define "trivial solvable radical" as R(X) = 1, where R(X) is the solvable radical (largest solvable normal subgroup) of X.
Optionally note the standard consequence that χ1(H) = χ1(G) forces |H| = |G|, since the sum of the squares of the entries of χ1(X) equals |X|.
refined_question: Let G and H be finite groups, and for any finite group X let χ1(X) denote the multiset of degrees χ(1) of all ordinary irreducible complex characters χ in Irr(X), counted with multiplicity. If χ1(H) = χ1(G) and the solvable radical R(G) of G is trivial (that is, R(G) = 1), must the solvable radical of H also be trivial?
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem 21.135. The nearby Archive entry 11.8(a) uses the same notation χ1(X) and records the solved simple-group case, explicitly observing that χ1(G) = χ1(H) implies |G| = |H|. The nearby new Problem 21.59 shows the same local theme in stronger special cases (almost simple and quasisimple G), which confirms that your draft is targeting this narrow recognition-by-χ1 question rather than a broader neighboring problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
